To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the hierarchical graph model proposed in [5] is the most succinct hierarchical model among those considered in this research and (ii) the hierarchical graph models are capable of representing a large class of graphs with hierarchical structures in a succinct fashion.

(1) the hierarchical graph model proposed by Harel and Tarjan [5] can be used to represent graphs with hierarchical structures; (2) the hierarchical graph representation proposed by Harel et al. [4] can be used for the purpose of representing graphs with hierarchical structure; (3) a hierarchical graph representation proposed in [5] can also be used to represent a graph with a hierarchical structure; (4) a hierarchical graph model can be used to describe graphs with hierarchical structures,
we present an algorithm that, given a hierarchical graph description, produces an orthogonal drawing of the graph in linear time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing algorithms for drawing graphs in a hierarchical fashion and for drawing hierarchical graphs. In particular,
drawing graphs that have a hierarchical structure, in a manner that preserves the hierarchical structure.
the study of the computational complexity of various geometric problems on graphs with hierarchical structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of drawing graphs with hierarchical representations is NP-complete.

the problem of drawing graphs in a hierarchical manner is an important problem and a number of succinct representations of graphs with hierarchical structures, as well as the drawing problems of graphs with such hierarchical representations, have been investigated in the literature.
a hierarchical design of a graph with hierarchical structure is possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a number of algorithms to construct orthogonal and straight-line drawings of graphs with hierarchical representations.
the problem of drawing hierarchical graphs is closely related to the problem of drawing graphs with succinct representations.

we have developed a systematic approach for studying the complexity of drawing graphs with succinct representations, and that we have obtained a number of results for various graph models, including the hierarchical tree models [4,5], the hierarchical graph models [6], and the hierarchical graph models with edge weights [7].
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hierarchical structure of a graph can be exploited to draw the graph in a succinct manner.

, for a large family of such hierarchical graph representations, we show that the graphs they represent can be drawn in the plane with a linear number of bends in straight-line fashion, with the exception of the hierarchical graph representation proposed in [5] where we show that the graph it represents can be drawn in straight-line fashion with a constant number of bends.
, in order to obtain a succinct representation, we need to give up on the ability to visualize the underlying graph.
